courses.title: Elliptic Operators & Boundary Problems

courses.title: Open Course — Modular Theory & Weights
courses.description: A research-level course developing integration and comparison for general weights, modular symmetry, standard forms, spatial derivatives, correspondences and expectations.
courses.coverage_note: 79 actual reading units from the frozen cumulative draft; seven additional planned units have no lesson source. All B1–B9 remain incomplete. This reader intake does not close proofs, certify complete source coverage or infer review from producer validation.
prerequisites: Arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces: completion, Riesz, bounded sesquilinear representation, adjoints and orthogonal projections.
Bounded C*-algebra continuous functional calculus, positive square roots, positivity and norm bounds.
Bicommutant theorem, bounded monotone nets, supports and bounded polar decomposition in arbitrary von Neumann algebras.
Ultraweak topology on bounded sets, separate multiplication continuity, normality of bounded positive maps equivalent to preservation of bounded increasing positive suprema.
General Hilbert spectral calculus for self-adjoint operators with exact Borel domains, bounded rectangular polar decomposition, finite-measure convergence and compact continuous approximation.
Conjugate-linear adjoints, closed operator graphs, analytic elements and strip/KMS arguments in the exact generality needed.
Enough states to detect positivity in arbitrary nonzero unital C*-algebras, including their norm-one property.
C*-bidual universal enveloping von Neumann algebra, canonical embeddings, isometric normal bidual inclusions, and same-norm weak-star-continuous second adjoints preserving compositions.
Bounded self-adjoint spectral projections inside a von Neumann algebra and norm approximation by spectral step functions.

Positive bounded maps between von Neumann algebras: preservation of bounded increasing positive suprema iff ultraweak continuity, with the positive same-norm preadjoint; provided by NP-04 at the recorded written-foundation boundary.
Concrete predual isometric duality, positive predual separation and span, normal-functional supports, inherited corner topology and ultraweak operations.
Sigma-strong and sigma-strong-star continuous duals equal the predual, with equal convex closures including the real self-adjoint versions.
Real/complex Hahn–Banach extension and locally convex separation, Banach–Alaoglu, weak compactness of Hilbert balls and Krein–Smulian for dual Banach spaces.

For the real-line and planar scalar integrals used in MA: Lebesgue integral bounds, sequential monotone and dominated convergence, absolutely integrable Fubini, the stated injective Borel changes of variables, finite-interval calculus, and integration by parts with integrable terms and verified endpoint limits. The exact source conditions and original application bridges are retained in the analytic packet.

For the scalar functions used in MA: rectangle and circle Cauchy formulas, local power series and primitives, rectangle Morera and its triangle application, identity on connected open sets, the boundary maximum principle on finite rectangles, and the original simple-pole calculation for the centered rectangles in MA05 and MA15. No arbitrary-cycle residue theorem is imported.

For every standard form (M,H,J,P) of an arbitrary von Neumann algebra, every normal semifinite faithful weight phi, and every directed net alpha_i in Aut(M) converging to alpha in the u-topology (norm convergence of f composed with alpha_i to f composed with alpha for every normal functional f), put C_phi(beta,t)=[D(phi composed with beta inverse):Dphi]_t. For every vector eta in H and every compact K in the real line, the supremum over t in K of ||(C_phi(alpha_i,t)-C_phi(alpha,t))eta|| tends to zero, and the same holds after taking adjoints. No separability, sigma-finiteness, faithful state, countable state family, ordered weights, bounded densities or strongly convergent inner lifts are assumed. The zero algebra is included.

Standard sigma-finite measurable Hilbert fields of separable complex fibres, including zero and variable dimensions; countable fundamental sections and measurable dimension strata; measurable scalar products, Gram-Schmidt and projections onto subspaces with specified measurable fundamental sections; bounded operator-field action, adjoints and norms; conjugate and direct-sum fields; bounded decomposable operators characterized as the commutant of the diagonal algebra; exact Hilbert direct-integral L2 spaces, finite-measure localization and almost-everywhere subsequences.

For a separably acting von Neumann algebra and a specified abelian von Neumann subalgebra of its center: a standard sigma-finite central decomposition with that subalgebra diagonal; countable-core localization for specified vector and operator families; fibrewise decomposable commutants and bicommutants; and almost-everywhere identification of two decompositions over the same diagonal structure.

Borel or analytic coding, followed by measurable selection after measure completion, for five countable constructions on a standard base: graph cores of closed right-multiplier relations; algebra pairs with fibrewise fundamental products; algebra sections whose left multipliers generate the fibre von Neumann algebras; locally bounded witnesses on positive-measure sets of nonfull fibres; and unitary fibre isomorphisms satisfying the countable graph, multiplier, involution, and rational modular tests.

Locally compact Hausdorff group analysis at arbitrary cardinality: left Haar Radon measure and its inversion/modular formulas, C_c-density and compactly supported approximate identities in L2, Radon product measure with L2 tensor identification, and nonunital Stone-Weierstrass for C0(G).

Every commutative complex C*-algebra, unital or nonunital, is isometrically *-isomorphic to C0 of its locally compact Hausdorff spectrum through its Gelfand transform; for a unital algebra the spectrum is compact.

For any locally compact Hausdorff space X with its Borel sigma algebra, every positive real-linear functional on real C_c(X) is represented by a unique regular Borel measure finite on compact sets. No compactness, metrizability, separability or sigma-compactness assumption is imposed.

Scalar Borel measure theory for standard Borel groups: finite and sigma-finite Radon–Nikodym derivatives and uniqueness, sigma-finite Tonelli/Fubini with Borel parameter integration, a countable Borel generator, and finite-partition L1 density. The joint derivative selection and its almost-everywhere convergence are proved in PF-38.

Standard-Borel Lusin–Souslin image theorem; compact inner approximation of finite Borel measures on Polish spaces; a Borel-isomorphism-to-Polish-group continuity principle; compact-group representation decomposition into finite-dimensional irreducibles. The regular-representation embedding, compact-neighborhood argument, category proof, and factor obstruction are given locally in PF-41–44.

For a faithful normal semifinite weight on any von Neumann algebra, global domination of X↦φ(aXa*) by φ is equivalent to a bounded modular negative-half-strip extension with endpoint norm at most one; under that condition, the right GNS action on every x in n_φ is Λ_φ(xa*)=J_φ σ^φ_{-i/2}(a) J_φ Λ_φ(x). Include the exact support-corner reduction for a nonfaithful normal semifinite weight.

Scalar real-line Plancherel, compact approximate identities, and the Weyl/multiplication commutant, including vector-valued Plancherel for arbitrary Hilbert multiplicity under Lebesgue measure; these are the exact harmonic inputs to the concrete dual average.

For an already existing faithful normal semifinite operator-valued weight T:A_+→B_hat_+, and any faithful normal semifinite scalar weight φ on B, the composite φ_hat◦T is n.f.s. and its modular group restricts to σ^φ on B. Only this forward direction is imported; it cannot depend on compatible-pair reconstruction.

For an n.f.s. trace τ on arbitrary semifinite Q, every normal weight on Q, including weights with a nonzero infinite part, is uniquely τ(h·−) for h in the full extended positive cone; the correspondence is additive, order preserving and normal.

For normal extended-positive operator-valued weights and a compatible real-line dual action, positive orbit integration commutes with normal extension and equivariant operator-valued maps on the entire extended positive cone; equality is checked against each positive normal functional, including infinite values.

For arbitrary n.f.s. scalar weights φ,ψ, the -i graph of u_t=[Dψ:Dφ]_t σ_t^φ has the exact oriented mixed finite-ideal identity ψ(az)=φ(zb), two-sided GNS ideal bounds, and extended-positive half-strip domination in the orientations of OR.6; include the necessary and sufficient graph criterion.

For an existing n.f.s. OVW, finite-domain matrix positivity places dot T(y*z) in the oriented mixed scalar ideal and identifies its scalar extension on the finite overlap; right spectral cutoffs extend the identity to every scalar GNS product without a countability assumption.

For the two strongly continuous cocycle-twisted isometric groups u^N and u^M in OR.5, prove that analytic graph inclusion G(u^N_-i)⊂G(u^M_-i) implies equality of their real actions on N through exponential-type elements and scalar Fourier uniqueness, without assuming N-invariance in advance. These mixed actions are not automorphism groups.

Von Neumann type decomposition and trace structure used in IX.4 Exercise 1: corners of semifinite and type-I algebras, absence of finite projections in type III, sigma-strong discontinuity of involution on an infinite corner, normal trace densities in type I, and the integrable-density centralizer cutdown lemma.
A von Neumann algebra is atomic exactly when its predual has the Radon-Nikodym property; trace classes and their l1-sums have that property, and it passes to closed subspaces.

For a separable factor M of type III_lambda with 0<=lambda<1 and a faithful strictly semifinite normal weight phi, the centralizer M_phi contains a maximal abelian subalgebra of M. Consequently M_phi' intersect M equals Z(M_phi).

For faithful normal semifinite weights alpha,beta and C>0, alpha<=C beta on the entire positive cone is equivalent to a bounded sigma-weakly continuous negative half-strip continuation of [Dalpha:Dbeta], with lower-boundary norm at most C^(1/2); include the finite-domain endpoint formula and both implications without sigma-finiteness.

With Fourier convention f-hat(p)=integral exp(ipt)f(t)dt, an element of a sigma-weakly continuous von Neumann algebra flow has Arveson spectrum in [0,infinity) exactly when its orbit extends boundedly and holomorphically to the lower half-plane. Include vector-valued Paley-Wiener support for entire functions of exponential type, invariance of support under differentiation and reflection, and the compact spectral-product inclusion.

For every factor M with separable predual, the functorial continuous core carries a strongly continuous dual action theta and a faithful normal semifinite trace tau with tau composed with theta_s equal to exp(-s) tau; its fixed algebra is M. The construction includes the canonical core unitary symbols of normal semifinite weights, their support corners, and positive normalized localizers a with the extended orbit integral I_theta(a)=1.

In the fixed continuous core, normal semifinite weights on M are in support-preserving bijection with positive affiliated grade-one operators h_phi. The correspondence has h_phi^(it)=phi^(it), implements sigma_t^phi on M, sends positive normal functionals exactly to tau-measurable grade-one operators, and its inverse is the normalized-localizer closed-form pairing used in equation (HL.11).

Fix a faithful normal state chi and its grade-one core density d. Embed X0=J_chi(M), with J_chi(x)(y)=chi(yx) and the transported operator norm, and X1=M_* with its predual norm, in the common ambient space M_*. For 0<p<1 prove a grade-preserving analytic construction identifying H(p) with [X0,X1]_p via T mapped to F_(T d^(1-p)), prove equality of the interpolation and homogeneous gauges, construct multilinear analytic families with exact endpoint bounds, and give actual complementary homogeneous representatives of bounded functionals. Approximation must preserve grades and converge in the displayed gauges and closed measurable products. Bounded spectral cutoffs alone do not preserve a positive real grade.

authorship.statement: Original scalar plot and proof diagram generated from assets/render_continuity.py; no source-book image is reproduced. Licensed under GFDL-1.2-or-later, with no invariant sections, front-cover texts or back-cover texts.

source_attribution: Mathematical proof: OA-MOD-OC-03 through OA-MOD-OC-08, equations (OC.3), (OC.9), and (OC.16) through (OC.20). The flow boxes concern automorphisms tending to the identity, with summand vector of norm one; the final line transfers to other faithful references and general limit automorphisms.

The scalar panel uses T = 1 and x = sqrt(lambda). Its positive-x curve is 2 sin(min(abs(log(x)), pi/2)); the separate kernel point has value one. The curve is a sampled plot of the exact scalar formula; the line 4 abs(x-1) is the proved bound.

Human antecedents: M. Takesaki, Theory of Operator Algebras II, sections IX.1 and IX.3; S. V. Stratila, Modular Theory in Operator Algebras, second edition, sections 3.11, 3.16 and 7.3 through 7.7. The diagram and plotting code are original.

courses.title: Constant-coefficient equations and solvability
courses.description: An advanced course on how polynomial symbols determine support, regularity, global solvability, Cauchy problems, and convolution equations.
courses.coverage_note: Ten substantive English lessons from frozen batch003. L001 has a bounded independent AI mathematical review under stated prerequisites; the other nine do not. All ten remain unadmitted and proof-open. Whole-course coverage, generality and prerequisite closure remain unfinished. Section anchors and reading routes do not certify theorem-level coverage.
prerequisites: distributions and Fourier transformation
Lebesgue spaces and functional analysis
multivariable and complex analysis

units.title: Fundamental solutions and the directions an equation uses
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): The prerequisites are distributional differentiation, convolution with a compactly supported distribution, tensor products of distributions, and elementary linear algebra. Two further distribution results are needed below: existence of a fundamental solution for every nonzero constant-coefficient operator, and the local expansion of a distribution supported on a hyperplane in normal derivatives of delta. Their exact statements are recalled where they are used. Basic references are Melrose's open *Differential Analysis* notes [Melrose], Grubb's open *Distributions and Operators* notes [Grubb], and the original existence theorem of Malgrange [Malgrange].

units.title: Measuring regularity with weighted Fourier spaces
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): Read Fundamental solutions and the directions an equation uses for the polynomial derivative norm. The analytic prerequisites are the Fourier transform on Schwartz functions and tempered distributions, Hölder's inequality, the \(L^1*L^p\) convolution inequality, and the duality of \(L^p\) for \(1\leq p<\infty\). The Fourier convention and its inverse are given in Fourier transforms, finite spectra and convex separation. Basic references are the open notes of Grubb [Grubb] and Melrose [Melrose], and Trèves's treatment of locally convex spaces and distributions [Treves].

units.title: Local regularity, sharp embeddings, and compactness
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): The prerequisite lesson is Measuring regularity with weighted Fourier spaces. We also use the Banach closed graph theorem, Arzelà–Ascoli, and smooth compact cutoffs on open subsets of Euclidean space. Basic references are Grubb [Grubb], Melrose [Melrose], and Rudin's treatment of the functional-analytic tools [Rudin]. All weights and Fourier normalizations are those of the preceding lesson. Write \(p'\) for the conjugate exponent, including the endpoints.

units.title: Regular kernels and changes in the equation
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): Read Measuring regularity with weighted Fourier spaces and Local regularity, sharp embeddings, and compactness first. We also use the distributional convolution identities discussed in Fundamental solutions and the directions an equation uses. The additional prerequisite is holomorphic averaging for polynomials, stated precisely below. Its construction belongs to the theory of Fourier–Laplace transforms. Basic references are the open treatments of distributions by Grubb [Grubb] and Melrose [Melrose], Malgrange's original existence paper [Malgrange], Hörmander's survey of existence and regularity [Hormander 1971], and Mantlik's work on dependence on a parameter [Mantlik].

units.title: Operator strength and local inverses
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): The prerequisites are Regular kernels and changes in the equation, Measuring regularity with weighted Fourier spaces, and Local regularity, sharp embeddings, and compactness. We use Plancherel's theorem to identify \(B_{2,1}\) with \(L^2\). Basic references are Grubb's open notes [Grubb], Melrose's open differential-analysis course [Melrose], and Malgrange's existence and approximation paper [Malgrange].

units.title: Rescaled symbols and stable strength
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): Read Operator strength and local inverses first. We use finite-dimensional norm equivalence and the fact that the product of two nonzero polynomials is nonzero. Basic references are Malgrange's work on differential and convolution equations [Malgrange], the Fourier analysis in Grubb's open notes [Grubb], and Trèves's treatment of constant-coefficient operators [Treves].

units.title: Freezing coefficients without losing strength
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): Read Operator strength and local inverses and Rescaled symbols and stable strength first. We also use the slowly moving weights constructed in Measuring regularity with weighted Fourier spaces, and the local-space and modulation estimates in Local regularity, sharp embeddings, and compactness. The kernel statement at the end assumes the Schwartz kernel theorem and the Fourier definition of a wave front set. Basic references are Melrose's open differential-analysis notes [Melrose], Grubb's distribution notes [Grubb], Trèves's treatment of locally convex spaces [Treves], and Mantlik's discussion of operators of equal strength [Mantlik].

units.title: The geometry of coefficients and strength
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): Read Rescaled symbols and stable strength and Operator strength and local inverses first. We use compactness in finite-dimensional complex vector spaces and the frequency-window estimates already proved there. Basic references are Mantlik's open paper on parameter-dependent operators [Mantlik], Malgrange's work on differential equations [Malgrange], and Trèves's constant-coefficient theory [Treves].

units.title: Positive symbols and energy estimates
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): Read Operator strength and local inverses and Measuring regularity with weighted Fourier spaces first. We use the Parseval–Plancherel theorem with the unnormalized Fourier transform. An exact open proof, including its extension from Schwartz functions to all of \(L^2\), is Grubb's Fourier chapter, Theorem 5.5 [Grubb]. The Schwartz identity is also the reading contract AN03-DEP-002 in the published Fourier prerequisite lesson. We use that identity with its stated normalization.

units.title: Approximation and global solvability from support geometry
dependencies: External entry conditions (not closed): The prerequisites are Local regularity, sharp embeddings, and compactness, Operator strength and local inverses, the Hahn–Banach separation theorem, and the Baire theorem for Fréchet spaces. The classical source for the approximation method is Malgrange's original paper [Malgrange]. The Fourier support results used at the entry to the argument are recorded precisely below; their distribution and Fourier proofs belong to the prerequisite course.

courses.title: Type III factors: central sequences, full factors and almost periodic states
courses.description: This course studies factors of type III through bounded sequences that asymptotically commute with the whole algebra and its normal states. It shows that a factor with separable predual is full, meaning that its inner automorphisms form a closed subgroup, exactly when all such sequences are trivial; it builds the invariants Sd and τ from almost periodic weights and the modular group; and it constructs full factors of type III₁ that have no almost periodic weight and are not crossed products of a semifinite algebra by a discrete abelian group. Basic references are [Connes 1974], [Connes 1973], [Connes 1976] and [Takesaki II].

courses.title: Injective factors
courses.description: This course classifies the injective factors with separable predual that are not of type III₁: the hyperfinite factor is the only injective factor of type II₁, there is only one of type II∞ and one of each type IIIλ with 0 < λ < 1, and the injective factors of type III₀ are the Krieger factors, classified by their flow of weights. It also shows that injectivity, approximate finite dimensionality, semidiscreteness and property P coincide for factors with separable predual (for type III₁ with the help of a later uniqueness theorem, used without proof), building on trace inequalities, property Γ and approximately inner and centrally trivial automorphisms. Basic references are [Connes 1976], [Connes 1973], [Takesaki III], [Brown–Ozawa] and [Connes 1994].

courses.title: Entropy of automorphisms
courses.description: These lessons define an entropy for automorphisms of operator algebras, the noncommutative counterpart of the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of ergodic theory. They start with automorphisms that preserve a trace, where the entropy tells apart the shifts of the hyperfinite II₁ factor built from matrices of different sizes, then treat automorphisms that preserve a state on a C*-algebra or a von Neumann algebra, and end with the entropy of lattice translations in quantum spin chains. Basic references are [Connes–Størmer 1975], [Connes–Narnhofer–Thirring 1987], [Neshveyev–Størmer 2006] and [Ohya–Petz 1993].

courses.title: Noncommutative integration and spatial theory
courses.description: This course develops integration on spaces that ordinary measure theory cannot see, such as the space of orbits of an ergodic group action or the leaf space of a foliation. It starts with the spatial derivative, which compares a weight on a von Neumann algebra with a weight on its commutant, and then builds transverse measures on measured groupoids, the von Neumann algebra of random operators, and the weights, formal dimension and index that come with them. Basic references are [Connes 1979], [Connes 1980a], [Connes 1982] and [Connes 1994].

courses.title: Global Langlands conjectures and functoriality
courses.description: The global side of the classical Langlands programme. The course sets up reductive groups and their L-groups, the Satake isomorphism for unramified groups and unramified L-factors, automorphic representations of general groups and their automorphic L-functions, and the analytic theory for GL_n (Godement–Jacquet, Rankin–Selberg, strong multiplicity one) as statements with their GL_1 and GL_2 cases recalled. It states the principle of functoriality and its known cases — symmetric powers and tensor products, base change for GL(2) (Langlands) and the Artin conjecture for two-dimensional representations (Langlands–Tunnell) — and the global reciprocity conjectures with the known cases. It states the modularity of elliptic curves over Q in its equivalent forms, outlines the Taylor–Wiles method, and proves the deductions that lead from modularity to Fermat's Last Theorem (given Ribet's theorem and Mazur's torsion theorem), to the analytic properties of L(E, s) and, with Serre's argument, to Sato–Tate from symmetric-power automorphy. It ends with the function-field case (statements) and an outlook on endoscopy and Arthur's classification. Deep theorems are stated exactly with references; the lessons prove the reductions, computations and deductions around them.
